<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `updateData (4 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **11** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `a11f9df0a8f0d143feb0387d35b31196b97fce3d` — the merge of head `2a20fe2d80044a52e88ee5238c238674d798c85a` into base `e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin a11f9df0a8f0d143feb0387d35b31196b97fce3d && git checkout a11f9df0a8f0d143feb0387d35b31196b97fce3d
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d 2a20fe2d80044a52e88ee5238c238674d798c85a && git checkout -B drift-repro e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d && git merge --no-ff 2a20fe2d80044a52e88ee5238c238674d798c85a

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs e611e2bdae9c1adb3d28d0e6b8e0cb4cb2f77c2d` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## 席位核对 — ACCEPT · `domain:spec` seat 2 (#18549) · session `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk` · 2026-10-15T08:12Z

This is the seat review of record for #23586 (p0, `security`; claim `6185927212`; triage `6184070020`, direction A) on head:

`2a20fe2d80`

It is not the contract review. That review is owed at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` because the published `409` body narrows (triage `6184070020`).

1. **Form.**
   - Draft to `main`. The first line is `Fixes #23586`, and `Clause-②: no` sits at the start of a line.
   - 3 files, +435/−11. Not governed: `check-governed-merges --pr 23628` reads NOT governed.
   - One patch changeset. The PR body, the changeset and the card comments stay at function level, under the disclosure rule.
2. **Against the routed direction.**
   - A stale token on a row the caller's RLS hides now answers exactly what the same request without a token answers: `404 RECORD_NOT_FOUND`, from the security layer's own producer, with no `currentVersion` and no `currentRecord`.
   - A conflict on a readable row carries the caller's FLS-masked read.
   - A matching token, or no token, is unchanged and issues no extra read.
   - `probeRecord` stays an existence question.
   - The fix is in one place, `assertVersionOf`, and serves both `updateData` and `deleteData`. The other two `probeRecord` callers are existence-only with no token, and the dev read each one.
3. **Pins and the red/green proof.**
   - The pins use the measured rig shape: real `ObjectQL`, a real SQL driver and the real `SecurityPlugin`.
   - They cover four groups × `PATCH`/`DELETE` × `RestServer`/dispatcher, and the dispatcher's thrown error is read too.
   - Red on the unfixed dist (8 of 16 failed, exactly the RLS and FLS rows); green after the fix (16/16).
4. **Gates.**
   - Locally on `2a20fe2d80`: 66 of 66 derived families ran with exit 0. One real red on the first pass (`check:query-options-erasure`) was fixed by typing the options.
   - Package suites on the merged head: `metadata-protocol`, `rest` and `runtime` are green.
   - CI on `2a20fe2d80`: 40 runs, 34 success, 6 skipped, none red.
5. **Accepted deviation.** The pin lives in `runtime`, not `rest`. `rest`'s test graph has no dispatcher, and `runtime` already holds the both-door OCC pins and real-`SecurityPlugin` rigs. It is a new file, and `runtime/src/domains/data.ts` is untouched, as the claim required.
6. **The dev's open questions.**
   - **Q1, `currentVersion` from the probe: A.** It keeps one meaning, the token the comparison ran on. No FLS rule keys on `updated_at` (0 hits).
   - **Q2, the Hono doors' hold on `currentRecord`: A, on its own card.** Once this lands, the producer's record is the caller's read, so #23587 (PR #23616) may lift its hold. This seat posts that on #23587 at landing. Nothing here touches `plugin-hono-server`.
   - **Q3, a `17.x` backport: answered by the maintainer.** "17.x 不再发版本", relayed in `6186913121`. No backport.
7. **Landing terms.** First a contract review PASS at `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` on the head, then every check green. Then the seat marks the PR ready and enables auto-merge. On merge #23586 closes, and its `pm:*` labels leave in the same act.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `2a20fe2d80044a52e88ee5238c238674d798c85a`
Local-runs: none

Inputs: card #23586 (body and every comment, 6183306689 through 6187598620), PR #23628 (body, its 3-file list, the net diff against the merge base `e611e2bdae` on `main`), and the 44 check-runs on the head. Judged against triage's routed direction A (6184070020), the measurement (6184039472) and the maintainer's no-17.x ruling as relayed (6186913121). Function level throughout, under the disclosure rule.

### ① Derived judgments

**Public surface.** `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation.updateData` and `deleteData` keep their signatures. `assertVersionOf` (now async, taking the request context), `assertVersionMatch` (taking the context) and the new `readAsCaller` are all `private`; nothing outside `protocol.ts` calls them (the only other mentions on the head are test and driver docblocks). `ConcurrentUpdateError` keeps its shape (`currentVersion: string | null`, `currentRecord: unknown`) and its export from `index.ts`. No export added, removed or renamed. No public-surface change. Right.

**Accept set.** No request served before is refused now: the matched-token and no-token paths are the old paths unchanged (the extra read sits on the mismatch branch only; pin 4 counts the engine reads). A hidden row's stale token moves from one error (`409`) to another (`404`); a readable row's `409` keeps its status, code and `currentVersion`, and `currentRecord` narrows to the caller's own read. No accept-set widening and no breaking narrowing: an undeclared disclosure removed, the declared read policy enforced at the conflict. Right.

**Every path that answers a version conflict.**
- `new ConcurrentUpdateError(` has exactly one site on the head, in `assertVersionOf`: the fixed one.
- `probeRecord` has four callers. `updateData` and `assertVersionMatch` (for `deleteData`) hand the token to `assertVersionOf`, so both are fixed by the one change. `assertRecordExists` (`updateManyData`, `batchData`'s update branch) and `batchData`'s upsert fork take no token, never hand the probed row to the caller (the upsert's response row is `engine.update`'s readback under the caller's context), and leave the write to the engine's own policy. Existence-only; right as left.
- `currentVersion` producers outside this path: `metadataConflictRefusal` (`METADATA_CONFLICT`, the `/meta` item doors: a keyed content hash of a metadata item's head, no record payload, not a record-data door) and `service-cluster-redis`'s KV version mismatch (an internal store, not a wire door). Both outside the class the card names; read, not findings.
- Doors: `structuredCodeAnswer`'s `CONCURRENT_UPDATE` arm in `packages/types` forwards only the fields the thrown error carries; `declaredConflictContext` in plugin-hono-server reads that arm, forwards `currentVersion` and still holds `currentRecord`; the runtime `/data` domain reads the token from the body, the query or `If-Match` and hands it to the protocol, with no producer of its own. Every door forwards the producer, so the fix at the producer reaches all of them. Right.

**A hidden row's stale-token answer against the no-token control, both doors.** On a mismatch the fix re-reads the row by id under the caller's context (`engine.findOne`, the same context spelling the write uses) and on absence throws `recordNotFoundError(object, id)` from `@objectstack/core`. That is the producer plugin-security's by-id write gate throws for a row absent under the caller's read (`security-plugin.ts`, `callerCannotReadAddressedRow` then `recordNotFoundError`), and that gate asks the same by-id caller-context question (`getCallerPreImage`). Same producer, same arguments: same status, code and message on both doors, with no `currentVersion` and no `currentRecord`. The pin asserts status and whole-body equality with the control on `RestServer` and the dispatcher, for `PATCH` and `DELETE`, and reads the dispatcher's thrown error for the two fields. Right. A hidden row whose token happens to match is unchanged: `assertVersionOf` returns and the write runs under the caller's policy, which answers its own `404`, so that case is indistinguishable too.

**A read that is refused rather than absent** (the object's read grant withheld): the fix propagates it. That is plugin-security's own rule for the write pre-image (#21771 ruling A: only absence is "cannot read"; a declared refusal keeps the write's answer). The refusal carries no row and no version, and the same caller's no-token write already answers an absent row and a present row differently, so nothing about existence is newly disclosed. Right.

**FLS.** `currentRecord` is the caller's own read, so the read door's field mask applies; the pin asserts equality with the caller's `findOne`, absence of the hidden field, and `currentVersion` equal to the stored token. Right.

**The existence probe stays the system's.** `probeRecord` is unchanged, so the #1994 by-id write policy keeps its place and the `rls-by-id-write` proof keeps its shape; Dogfood Regression Gate is green on the head. Right.

**Pins.** One new file in `packages/runtime/src/domains/`, on the measured rig shape: a real ObjectQL over a real SQL driver with the real `SecurityPlugin` started, one RLS policy and one FLS rule on one object, a plain second object. Four groups, `PATCH` and `DELETE`, `RestServer` and the dispatcher: 16 cases; the dispatcher's throw is rendered through `declaredEnvelopeForThrow`, the Hono hosts' exit. The report reads 8 of 16 red on the unfixed dist and 16 of 16 green after; Test Core and its six shards are green on the head. Read as the gate verdicts, not re-run here.

**Gates on the head.** 44 check-runs, all completed. The five required contexts (Lint & Repo Gates, TypeScript Type Check, Test Core, Build Core, Governed Surface Queue Guard) and every other non-skipped run conclude `success`; the skipped runs are path or schedule selectors (Console Pin Gate, the Dogfood shards, Dogfood Verify CLI, Build Docs, Temporal Conformance, the opt-in tarball smoke). None red.

**Disclosure rule.** The PR body, the changeset and the pin file's docblock stay at function level: mechanism and answers, no reproduction recipe beyond what the card itself states, no record samples. Right.

### ② Semver level

The changeset `.changeset/23586-occ-conflict-caller-visibility.md` grades `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` `patch` and carries `Clause-②: no` with no arm; the PR body carries `Clause-②: no` at the start of a line. Check Changeset is green.

- `patch` is truthful: a bug fix in a released package. Nothing authorable or exported is removed or renamed, so no migration text and no ADR-0087 marker is owed.
- `Clause-②: no` is truthful: the card widens no accept set and no public surface, which is the question the line answers. What narrows is an error body for a caller the declared policy already denies: the declared boundary enforced, not moved (triage 6184070020). The `(narrowing)` arm, which declares a breaking narrowing of an accepted shape, is rightly absent; the first claim's `no (narrowing)` was superseded by the dispatching claim's `Clause-②: no`.
- `assertVersionOf` becoming async narrows no public signature: it is `private`, both callers await it, and a private member carries no signature on the published declaration file.
- One package in the changeset is right: `rest`, `runtime` and `plugin-hono-server` change no code and take the narrowed answer through the dependency.

### ③ Boundary flags

**Dev deviations** (report 6187368395):
1. The pin lives in `packages/runtime`, not `packages/rest`. Answered: `rest`'s test graph has no `HttpDispatcher`; `runtime` already holds the both-door OCC pins and real-`SecurityPlugin` rigs; the claim's ⛔ list does not name `runtime`; new file only, and `runtime/src/domains/data.ts` is untouched. Right.
2. Model-free commit trailers. Verified on the four branch commits and the merge commit: `Claude-Session:` plus `Co-authored-by: Claude`, no model identifier. Right; AGENTS.md outranks the harness note.
3. The dev's own container re-pointed its shared checkout before editing. A process note inside that session; nothing in the diff. Not a contract matter.

**PR-body acceptance notes:** the Hono doors untouched (right under the claim's file surface; the producer's narrowed answer reaches them); `currentVersion` taken from the system probe (Q1 below); a caller-context read that throws propagates (judged right in ①).

**`open_questions`:**
- Q1, `currentVersion` when an FLS rule hides `updated_at`: answered A, as recommended. The token is the comparison's own subject and the handle a guarded write must hold; the card's acceptance and direction A both keep `currentVersion`'s meaning; no field-permission entry keys on `updated_at` (the dev's grep, 0 hits). Not escalated.
- Q2, lifting the Hono doors' hold on `currentRecord`: answered A, on #23587's own PR once this lands. Triage 6184070020 holds #23587's ⛔ until this card lands, and plugin-hono-server is outside this PR's surface. Not escalated.
- Q3, a 17.x backport: answered by the maintainer's ruling relayed in 6186913121. No 17.x release, no backport branch, no tag; the changeset states what closes at function level so a 17.x user reads it in the 18 notes. Closed.

Nothing escalated.

Reviewed-by: `session_01LFqdRsuM5nkqoJdHd5ztVk`
